subject: Energy
title: Petrochemicals and Modern Life
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Petrochemicals and Modern Life.

hook.text: Oil isn't just burned—it's transformed into plastics, fertilizers, medicines, and thousands of chemical products.

buildup.text: Petrochemical refineries crack crude oil into ethylene, propylene, and other building blocks of modern materials.

discovery.text: Plastics (from the 1950s) are made from oil—packaging, clothing, electronics, and medical devices all depend on them.

twist.text: The Haber-Bosch process uses natural gas to make ammonia fertilizer—feeding roughly half the world's population.

climax.text: Oil as a chemical feedstock may persist even after we stop burning it—the chemistry isn't the climate problem.

punchline.text: Oil built the material world—not just the energy one.

quiz.question: What does the Haber-Bosch process produce from natural gas?
